record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: For a C^∞-generic Hamiltonian H near the integrable model on T^*T^n and for a generic ergodic minimizing measure μ in the sense of Mather, is the restricted flow f^H_t|_{supp(μ)} on H^{-1}(1) hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: 2. For the C∞ -generic H and the generic ergodic minimal measure µ of Mather [MA2], is the ﬂow fH t|supp(µ) on H−1(1) a hyperbolic ﬂow ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ and let $T^*\mathbb{T}^n$ denote its cotangent bundle, endowed with the canonical symplectic structure. Consider a Hamiltonian $H: T^*\mathbb{T}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ that is a $C^\infty$-small perturbation of an integrable Tonelli Hamiltonian $H_0(q,p)=\tfrac{1}{2}\langle A p, p\rangle$ (with $A$ a positive definite symmetric matrix), and let $(f^H_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ denote the Hamiltonian flow generated by $H$. For a fixed cohomology class (or rotation vector), Mather's variational principle produces ergodic action-minimizing probability measures supported on the energy level $H^{-1}(1)$; call any such measure an ergodic minimizing measure $\mu$ in the sense of Mather, and write $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$ for its support.

Question: Is it true that for a $C^\infty$-generic Hamiltonian $H$ (in the sense of a residual subset in the $C^\infty$ topology) near $H_0$, and for a generic ergodic Mather-minimizing measure $\mu$, the restricted flow $f^H_t|_{\mathrm{supp}(\mu)}$ on $H^{-1}(1)$ is a hyperbolic flow (i.e., $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$ is a uniformly hyperbolic invariant set for the flow)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of generic hyperbolicity of supports of Mather-minimizing measures for generic Tonelli Hamiltonians on $T^*\mathbb{T}^n$ remains open in general. Partial results exist: Le Calvez established uniform hyperbolicity of generic Aubry-Mather sets for exact symplectic twist maps (essentially the $n=1$ / surface case); Arnaud and others have shown C^1-regularity results when Lyapunov exponents vanish; and there are results showing that perturbations can make the Mather set consist of hyperbolic periodic orbits in certain settings. No full resolution in arbitrary dimension was located.

status_evidence.title: Green bundles, Lyapunov exponents and regularity along the supports of invariant measures
status_evidence.snippet: For a Tonelli Hamiltonian with an ergodic minimizing probability measure whose Lyapunov exponents are all zero, the support of the measure is C^1-regular at almost every point.
status_evidence.claim: Partial regularity results exist for minimizing measures, but full generic hyperbolicity in higher dimensions is not established.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian Systems, MSRI Publications Volume 72 (Cheng-Xue)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of generic properties of Mather sets and their hyperbolicity in higher-dimensional Tonelli Hamiltonian systems.
status_evidence.claim: The hyperbolicity of generic Mather sets in higher dimensions is treated as an ongoing research direction.
